manual.title: How to read the scanner
manual.intro: A clear guide to what is on the chart and how to trade what you see. Use the menu on the right to jump to any section.

overview.title: What the Cypher Scanner is
overview.lead: The Cypher Scanner reads the chart on several layers at once: trend, momentum, reaction levels and volatility. When enough of those layers agree on the same candle, a clear signal prints on the screen. A green B to buy, a purple S to sell. You do not read indicators, you read the result.
overview.p: The trade arrives fully formed. The entry, the stop loss, and three take-profit targets are worked out for you and drawn on the chart. Your only job is to act when the conditions line up, and to wait when they do not.
overview.c1b: Trend, momentum, levels and volatility read together, so you are not juggling a dozen indicators.
overview.c2b: Forex, gold, indices and crypto. The scanner adapts its levels to whatever you load.
overview.c3b: From scalping the 5m to swinging the daily, the reads are the same. You pick the clock.

whoAndWhen.title: Who it is for, and when to use it
whoAndWhen.p1: Cypher was built for two kinds of trader: the one starting out who wants the chart to make sense, and the one who already trades and wants cleaner setups with less screen time.
whoAndWhen.c1b: Everything is colour coded and labelled. Green means up, purple means down, a letter on the candle means it is time. Learn a handful of reads and you can follow along from day one.
whoAndWhen.c2b: Use it as a confirmation layer. Filter setups, time entries more precisely, and read multi-timeframe context at a glance.
whoAndWhen.p2: It also adapts to whatever the market is doing right now.
whoAndWhen.c3b: Price is moving with momentum. Cypher highlights pullbacks and continuation entries so you join the trend instead of chasing it.
whoAndWhen.c4b: Price is stuck between two levels. Cypher marks the top and bottom so you can fade the edges rather than guess.
whoAndWhen.c5b: A strong trend retraces into the inner band. These are the cleanest entries, and Cypher flags the re-entry.

markets.title: Markets and timeframes
markets.p1: Cypher works across every major asset class and adapts its reaction levels automatically. You do not change settings between gold and indices, or between forex and crypto. One tool, every market.
markets.c1b: Majors, crosses and emerging-market pairs. Low-priced and high-priced pairs alike.
markets.c2b: Spot gold, silver and other metals get their own tuning for higher-priced assets.
markets.c3b: S&P, Nasdaq, Dow and the rest. Wider reaction levels suit how indices move.
markets.c4b: Bitcoin, Ethereum and the large-cap alts, using the wider levels that suit crypto volatility.
markets.callout: Begin with Gold (XAU/USD), NAS100 and US30 on the 15m, 1h and 4h. They give the cleanest reads. Once you are comfortable, add more pairs and timeframes from there.
markets.p2: Any style works. Scalpers read the short timeframes the same way as the long ones. Day traders sit in the sweet spot on the 15m to 1h. Swing traders take fewer, larger setups on the higher timeframes. The routine never changes, only the clock.

flag.title: The Flag: your signal
flag.lead: The Flag is the main trigger. It is the moment the system's reads agree on the same candle. When that happens, a single letter prints: a green B for buy, a purple S for sell, on the candle it happens.
flag.p: Behind the letter, three things line up on the same candle: the fast trend lines cross, the candle closes in the trade's direction, and the underlying flow at the bottom of the chart is not pointing the other way. The instant those agree, the Flag prints. You do not track any of it. You wait for the letter.
flag.callout: The Flag sits just off the candle, the buy below and the sell above, so it never hides behind price. It fires once when a fresh setup lines up, rather than repeating while a single move plays out.

reversalBands.title: Reversal Bands
reversalBands.p1: Cypher draws adaptive bands that move with volatility and mark where price is most likely to turn.
reversalBands.i1: Inner band: the first level of support and resistance, where pullbacks tend to end.
reversalBands.i2: Outer band: the high-probability reversal zone, where the bigger turns happen.
reversalBands.p2: The space between the bands is tinted green or purple so you can see at a glance which side you are on. The strongest entries happen where price reacts to a band and the rest of the system agrees.

keyLevels.title: Key Levels
keyLevels.p1: Cypher draws the round-number price levels that large players reference for orders. They form zones of support and resistance you can see coming well in advance.
keyLevels.i1: Red zones above price act as resistance.
keyLevels.i2: Blue zones below price act as support.
keyLevels.i3: Grey lines mark the levels, with a coloured glow showing which side of price they sit.
keyLevels.p2: The spacing adapts to your timeframe and market. When a band touch lines up with a key level, the odds of a clean reaction go up.

pivots.title: Pivots and Fair Value Gaps
pivots.p1: Pivots are well-known reaction zones calculated from the previous session. They add a third layer of support and resistance.
pivots.i1: Green lines below price are the support pivots.
pivots.i2: Purple lines above price are the resistance pivots.
pivots.i3: Inner pivots are nearby targets. Outer pivots are extreme stretch zones.
pivots.callout: On the 15m and above, Cypher marks Fair Value Gaps as translucent boxes: imbalances left behind when price moves too fast. Markets tend to come back and fill them, so an unfilled gap becomes a target area.

trendTable.title: Trend Table
trendTable.p1: The Trend Table sits in the top-right corner and reads the market on several timeframes at once, so you can see which way each layer points in a single glance.
trendTable.i2: Green means that timeframe is bullish, purple means bearish.
trendTable.i3: Your current timeframe is highlighted, so you always know where you sit.
trendTable.callout: Each column reads from that timeframe's own last closed candle, so a column shows the same thing no matter which chart you are on. The most useful read is your trading timeframe against the one above it. When both agree, you have the wind behind you.

pulseLine.title: The Pulse Line
pulseLine.p1: The Pulse Line lives in its own pane below the chart, like a heart monitor for momentum. It is there for confirmation, not as the trigger, and it often moves before price does.
pulseLine.c1b: Is it pointing the same way as your trade? Up for buys, down for sells. The basic check.
pulseLine.c2b: A large dot prints when momentum hands over. One of the strongest early cues.
pulseLine.c3b: When the Pulse Line moves the opposite way to price, a D prints. The strongest reversal cue Cypher gives.
pulseLine.c4b: A row of bars shows the underlying bias. Green bullish, purple bearish, grey mixed.

barColour.title: Bar colour and arrows
barColour.p1: Three smaller features sit on the candles and quietly do a lot of the work.
barColour.c1b: Every candle is outlined by the underlying read. Green is bullish flow, purple is bearish, grey is mixed or waiting. This is one of the conditions behind the Flag.
barColour.c2b: Small arrows for quick continuation entries inside a strong trend. Handy for adding to winners or taking pullback re-entries.
barColour.c3b: Larger arrows when price breaks a recent swing with volume behind it, labelled with the volume strength.

setups.title: The three setups
setups.p1: Almost every Cypher trade is one of three types. Knowing which one you are in tells you what to confirm and what to ignore.
setups.c1b: Price is moving sideways between a top and a bottom. Trade the bounces and fade the extremes.
setups.c2b: Price is moving one way. Wait for a pullback to the inner band, then enter on the continuation when the Flag fires.
setups.c3b: Price has run into a major band and momentum is exhausted. Catch the turn as the Flag fires the other way.

routine.title: The five-rule routine
routine.p1: Whichever setup you are in, the routine is the same. Run through it in order. If a rule fails, you skip the trade. If they all pass, you take it.
routine.s1b: Identify which of the three setups is in front of you. The bands and the Trend Table do most of that work for you.
routine.s2b: Wait for the letter. No B or S, no trade. This is the moment the system tells you the pieces line up, and it anchors every other check.
routine.s3b: Confirm momentum agrees: its direction, a secondary-signal cross, or a fresh divergence D.
routine.s4b: Make sure price is at a meaningful zone: a reversal band, a key level, a pivot, or an unfilled gap. Two lining up is good, three is excellent.
routine.s5b: Read the entry, stop and targets on the chart, place the trade with proper risk to reward, then manage to plan.

tradePlan.title: Your trade plan: entry, stop, targets
tradePlan.p1: The moment the Flag fires, the levels appear on the right edge of the chart. You do not calculate. You read.
tradePlan.r1v: The price marked at the Flag candle. Enter at market, or wait for a small pullback into it for a tighter stop.
tradePlan.r2v: Sits at the most recent swing: the swing low for a buy, the swing high for a sell. If price closes through it, the read is invalid and you exit.
tradePlan.r3v: TP1, TP2 and TP3 sit at one, two and three times the distance from your entry to the stop. The same clean risk to reward on every market.
tradePlan.callout: A common approach is to take part off at TP1, more at TP2, and trail the rest toward TP3. Moving your stop to entry once TP1 is hit protects the trade. If the bar colour flips against you before TP2, take the rest off at market.

faq.title: Quick answers
faq.r1k: Do I have to watch all of this?
faq.r1v: No. Wait for the letter. Everything else is context that makes a signal stronger or weaker.
faq.r2k: How many signals will I get?
faq.r2v: It depends on the pair and timeframe. The 15m, 1h and 4h give fewer, cleaner reads than the very low timeframes.
faq.r3v: Stand down, or wait for them to line up. The best trade is sometimes no trade.
faq.r4k: Where do the entry, stop and targets come from?
faq.r4v: They are drawn for you automatically the moment the Flag fires.
faq.r5k: Can I use it on any market?
faq.r5v: Yes. Cypher adapts its levels to forex, gold, indices and crypto without changing settings.
